character_facts: Bari is a boy or youth with long light-colored hair.
Bari's father is wealthy or powerful enough to obtain an extraordinarily expensive resurrected animal.
Bari is emotionally affected by the gift and longs for renewed enjoyment of life.
Shazam is a resurrected white horse that becomes obedient to Bari after being named and fed sugar.
continuity_links: The page centers on Bari's relationship with his father through the gift of the horse.
The narration frames this as a turning point leading to Bari's renewed engagement with life on the new planet.
dialogue_meaning: A narrator stresses the rarity of the horse: it is a revived specimen of a breed extinct for twenty millennia.
The narrator emphasizes the immense expense and technical effort required to bring the horse back to life.
The father presents the horse as a personal gift for Bari and gives practical advice for bonding with it.
Bari tells his father that the gift is beyond words and that riding it would bring back his appetite for life.
The narration says Bari names the horse Shazam, becomes its accepted master, and finds renewed happiness riding it.
locations: A spacecraft landing or unloading area
A technologically advanced reception or hangar-like setting
The garden paradise of the family's new planet
lore_facts: Horses have been extinct for 20,000 years since the Sixth World War.
The Imperial Palace maintains a genetic museum preserving the genes of extinct species.
A horse can be recreated through advanced scientific labor by techno-scientists.
Reviving this horse cost 100 tons of gold.
Bari's family is living on a new planet described as a garden paradise.
Large flying creatures inhabit or pass over that planetary landscape.
plot_events: Narration explains that the animal is a living horse, an extinct breed preserved through imperial genetic conservation.
The horse is presented as an extremely costly scientific reconstruction created by techno-scientists.
An older man gives the horse to a boy named Bari as a gift meant specifically for him.
The boy is overwhelmed with gratitude and says riding the animal would restore his joy in life.
The horse accepts Bari after he names it 'Shazam' and feeds it sugar.
Bari begins a new, happier phase of life by riding Shazam through the paradise-like environment of their new planet.
uncertainties: The father's personal name is not clearly legible on the page image; he is identified only as Bari's father.
Some minor background figures and robots are not individually identifiable.

visual_summary: A narrated flashback page shows a white horse being unloaded from a spacecraft and handled by technicians in a futuristic setting. A young long-haired boy and an older silver-haired man receive the animal, with small robots and attendants nearby. The boy later rides the horse named Shazam across a lush landscape with large winged creatures overhead.
